Adjournment

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not
listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be
taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each
speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Time may be surrendered by deferring (1) one minute to another speaker,
not to exceed a total of (8) eight minutes. The speaker wishing to defer time must be present when the item is
heard. In order to be recognized and present an item, each speaker must complete and submit to the Recording
Secretary a Request to Speak form prior to the beginning of the item being announced by the Chair (forms are
available at the entrance to the meeting room). Speakers are taken in the order slips are submitted.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting
where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public
discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning
decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of
the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is
 Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission  Page 3 of 3  September 11, 2025

desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may
indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to
adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission
following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public
speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral
Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting
with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral
Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall
follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are
on file in the City Clerk Department, Malibu City Hall, 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, California and are
available for public inspection during regular office hours which are 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through
Thursday, and 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday. Written materials distributed to the Commission within 72 hours
of the Commission meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution (Government Code
Section 54957.5(b)(2). Copies of staff reports and written materials may be purchased for $0.10 per page.
Pursuant to State law, this agenda was posted at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the
deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance
with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please
contact Environmental Sustainability Director Yolanda Bundy, (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours
prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.
[28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was
posted in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 10th day of September 2025 at 11:50
a.m.

  Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk

MOTION  Chair Shenkman nominated Bill Sampson for Vice Chair. The question
  was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  In response to Chair Shenkman, City Clerk Pettijohn clarified that the
  minutes from the March 13, 2008 meeting were prepared by the recording
  secretary at the time based on notes taken at the meeting. She stated that
  the minutes needed to be approved by the Commission to be entered into
  the official record.

  In response to Commissioner Blackman, Interim City Attorney Rusin
  clarified that no recording of the meeting was available for the
  Commissioners to review.

  Commissioner Grisanti stated he was present at the March 13, 2008
  meeting and Recording Secretary Linden took reliable notes.

  Commissioner Blackman noted that there were no significant decisions
  made at the March 13, 2008 meeting.

  Chair Shenkman stated he reviewed the comments from former City
  Attorney Hogin at the March 13, 2008 meeting and expressed concern that
  she was incorrect about the scope and role of the Commission. He stated
  that approving the minutes did not mean the Commissioners agreed with
  the statements in the minutes.

  In response to Chair Shenkman, City Clerk Pettijohn confirmed that
  voting to approve the minutes did not mean the Commissioners verified
  the statements made at the meeting were accurate.

  Chair Shenkman expressed concern that there were many statements by
  members of the public at the March 13, 2008 meeting regarding rent
  increases, but another meeting was not scheduled at the time to investigate
  this.

  Chair Shenkman opened the floor for public comment on the Consent
  Calendar. As there were no speakers present, he returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

MOTION  Chair Shenkman moved, and Commissioner Blackman seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion
  carried 3-1, Vice Chair Sampson abstained.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Commissioner Orientation
  Recommended action: Receive and file commissioner orientation.

  Deputy City Attorney Lomakin explained the Commission’s role under
  the Malibu Municipal Code and its role as a quasi-judicial body.

  Chair Shenkman opened the floor for public comment. As there were no
  speakers present, he returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  In response to Commissioner Blackman, Deputy City Attorney Lomakin
  clarified that the Commission may not be in a position to review or make
  changes to the ordinance. She confirmed state law will supersede local
  regulations. She stated State law did not preempt on rent stabilization
  issues the State had recognized this as an acceptable use of cities’ police
  powers.

  In response to Vice Chair Sampson, Deputy City Attorney Lomakin
  explained that the Commission had limited powers and duties under the
  Malibu Municipal Code and had to work within the framework of existing
  regulations.

  In response to Chair Shenkman, Deputy City Attorney Lomakin stated the
  powers described in the code are exclusive. She stated the powers and
  duties section does limit the Commissions’ powers and duties to reviewing
  rent adjustment applications and possibly hearing appeals of a rent
  determination at the time a mobilehome park registers with the City. She
  stated the Council would have the power to give the Commission greater
  discretion.

  Chair Shenkman discussed the Commission’s powers to conduct
  investigations to obtain such information as is necessary to carry out its
  duties. He discussed the rent adjustment reports the parks are required to
  file with the City and residents’ right to submit applications for rent
   Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission Meeting Minutes
  June 30, 2025
  Page 4 of 8
  ______________________
  decreases. He asked if the Commission could review and investigate the
  reports filed with the City.

  In response to Chair Shenkman, Deputy City Attorney Lomakin stated the
  Commission would have the authority to investigate after an application is
  filed.

  Chair Shenkman stated he disagreed with that analysis.

  In response to Commissioner Grisanti, Interim City Attorney Rusin
  confirmed the City Council had formed a Mobilehome Park Rent Control
  Regulation Ad Hoc Committee to review the Mobilehome Park Rent
  Control Ordinance.

  City Clerk Pettijohn confirmed Mayor Pro Tem Silverstein and
  Councilmember Stewart had been appointed to the Mobilehome Park Rent
  Control Regulation Ad Hoc Committee.

  In response to Chair Shenkman, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated he
  would follow-up on the progress of the Mobilehome Park Rent Control
  Regulation Ad Hoc Committee and could provide an update to the
  Commission.

  Vice Chair Sampson stated he did not agree with the Deputy City
  Attorney’s interpretation of the Commission’s powers.

  Interim City Attorney Rusin stated the goal was to have the Commission
  function and be helpful to the City.

  Chair Shenkman received and filed the commissioner orientation without
  objection. He noted a portion of the Commission expressed disagreement
  with the interpretation of the municipal code.

ITEM 2  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Robert Heinz discussed living in the Point Dume Club and the lack of
  other affordable housing in the City. He expressed concern that space
  rents could be increased and require many residents to move out of the
  City. He requested the Commissioners support rent control.

  Sandra McHenry discussed her residency in Point Dume Club, her
  husbands health concerns requiring them to spend more time close to
  doctors in Fresno. She stated she would not be able to continue to
  maintain her residence if there was a change to rent control, especially
  changes to subleases.

Katarina Vinegrad stated she had lived in Point Dume Club since 2014.
She discussed the lack of affordable housing for ordinary people in the
City. She stated she could not afford a significant rent increase. She
discussed the new corporate ownership of the Point Dume Club.

Michael Motrales declined the opportunity to speak

Flora Sanchez discussed the importance of protecting the senior
population of Malibu.

Janet Birch stated mobilehomes were meant to provide low income
housing, but her space rent was $2,200. She discussed increased water
bills including new fees. She discussed the enforcement of infractions and
increased rent for subleases.

Howard Ferguson welcomed the new Commissioners.  He discussed
changes in the Point Dume Club.

Candace Bowen-Ferguson, Vice President of Point Dume Club Residence
Association, stated she submitted comments from other residents for the
record. She read comments from Dru Ann Jacobson, and Betty Thomas.
She thanked the Commissioners for the service.

Kelly McKinna discussed her search for affordable housing and her move
to the City. She discussed the importance of maintaining affordable
housing in the City to have a diverse community. She thanked the
Commissioners for their service.

Villani Kadic discussed her move to the mobilehome park in 1972 when it
was senior housing. She discussed residents who had passed or moved
away, and the few number of long-term locals remaining. She stated if
rent increased significantly, she would have to move out of the
community.

Bracken Carter described living in Paradise Cove and now Point Dume
Club with her three kids. She discussed the limited affordable housing
and low enrollment in Malibu public schools.  She thanked the
Commissioners for their service.

COMMISSIONER INQUIRIES

Commissioner Grisanti described the current limits on rent increases,
which allowed a 2-5% increase per year depending on the consumer price
index. He discussed the high levels of inflation in recent years and stated
the current inflation rate was lower. He stated rents could not be
   Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission Meeting Minutes
  June 30, 2025
  Page 6 of 8
  ______________________
significantly increased in short term but could increase substantially over
time if there is high inflation.

Commissioner Blackman discussed the promise of affordable housing that
was made when the City was formed. He discussed the importance of
maintaining that promise while also looking at the big picture.

Vice Chair Sampson described his family’s move to Malibu in 1980 when
prices were more affordable. He discussed differences of opinion between
himself and Chair Shenkman and the BBK attorneys. He addressed the
public speakers and stated he understood their concerns. He discussed his
history as a resident his involvement in the community. He promised to
honor the rent control ordinance.

In response to Vice Chair Sampson, Ms. Birch stated the new water fees
were imposed by the Point Dume Club park owners.

Vice Chair Sampson thanked the public speakers.

In response to Chair Shenkman, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated he
would have to review the General Plan to determine if the mobilehome
parks were designated as low-income housing.

In response to Chair Shenkman, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated staff
would need more information on the new water fees to determine if it
required approval from the Commission. He asked Ms. Birch to provide
her information to City Clerk Pettijohn.

Chair Shenkman stated if this water fee was applied to all tenants the
Commission should be able to address it without requiring individual
applications from each tenant. He thanked the public for attending the
meeting and discussed the importance of public participation. He
discussed the March 13, 2008 meeting minutes and the public comments
and legal advice provided at that meeting. He discussed the lack of
follow-up from that meeting. He requested consensus to set a new
meeting date and provide direction on agenda items. He stated based on
his reading of the ordinance, sublessors can only get a 15% premium and
if there was an increase beyond that it needed to be addressed by the
Commission. He requested consensus to bring back an item to discuss
posting an application form. He discussed the sale of the Point Dume
Club to a corporation. He discussed AB 768 and disclosed that the
Assemblymember was a friend of his. He stated the bill died in committee
and discussed the impacts it would have had eliminating rent control on
subleased mobilehomes. He discussed the intent and arguments in favor
of the bill. He stated the City needed to get ahead on this issue before it is
imposed by the legislature. He requested consensus to bring back an item
   Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission Meeting Minutes
  June 30, 2025
  Page 7 of 8
  ______________________
  to discuss AB 768. He requested consensus to bring back an item to
  investigate all space rents based on historic data.

MOTION  Chair Shenkman moved, and Vice Chair Sampson second a motion to
  review the Mobilehome Park Rent Control Regulations and recommend
  changes.

  Commissioner Grisanti asked if each Commissioner could speak to their
  appointing Councilmember about the ordinance.

  In response to Commissioner Grisanti, City Clerk Pettijohn suggested the
  Commission could request the City Council direct the ordinance review to
  the Commission during Commissioner Reports at the next City Council
  meeting.

  Interim City Attorney Rusin stated Commissioners could speak with
  Councilmembers as long as it did not create a serial meeting. He
  suggested if the Commission intended to expand its role beyond what is
  specifically directed in the code it may be appropriate to bring an item to
  the City Council.

  Chair Shenkman stated the Commissioners could speak to
  Councilmembers individually while also reviewing the ordinance at the
  Commission.

  Commissioner Blackman proposed a joint meeting with the Council and
  Commission.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Chair Shenkman moved, and Commissioner Blackman seconded a motion
  to bring back a report on past rent increases and the documentation on file
  with the City. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  In response to Vice Chair Sampson, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated
  staff would look into the water fees.

  Chair Shenkman discussed scheduling meetings and the importance of
  balancing public participation and staff availability. He suggested
  adjourning the meeting to a specific date and time.

  City Clerk Pettijohn requested the Commission not adjourn to a specific
  date and time. She stated staff could not confirm space and staff
  availability for the next meeting right now.

  In response to Chair Shenkman, City Clerk Pettijohn stated she was not
  certain how much time would be needed for staff to gather the historic
  records the Commission requested.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 2:39 p.m., Chair Shenkman moved, and Vice Chair Sampson seconded
  a motion to adjourn the meeting and hold the next meeting within 30 days
  subject to scheduling with City staff.

  KEVIN SHENKMAN, Chair

Subject:  Process for Annual Formula Rent Increase

RECOMMENDED ACTION:  Receive and file.

DISCUSSION:  Each year, in compliance with Malibu Municipal Code (M.M.C.)
Section 5.16.090, mobile home park owners are eligible to increase space rents. The
annual formula rent increase is based on the 12 months percent change in the
Consumer Price Index (CPI-U) from November to November as reported by the United
States Bureau of Labor Statistics for All Urban Consumers in the Los Angeles-Riverside-
Orange County statistical region. The City posts a public notice each December for the
upcoming calendar year, providing copies to the management of each of the
mobilehome parks in the City. In compliance with the approved CPI-U, owners may
increase space rents on an individual basis.

Staff will provide a report that thoroughly explains this process for the benefit of the
Commission.
